title: Latency decomposition by serving path and IO mode
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Build a cross-cutting dashboard and telemetry plumbing that decomposes token/response latency by: model, API route (text/generate, chat, embeddings, rerank), serving path (hosted, dedicated, private), and IO mode (streaming vs sync). Provide p50/p95/p99 summaries and a heatmap-style view for regression hunting. Include tracing hooks to connect trace spans to model shards and telemetry tags for routing policy and fallback chains.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency for each model x route combination and allows filtering by serving path (hosted/dedicated/private)
UI has toggle to compare streaming vs sync latencies side-by-side and an aggregated delta column
Each data point links to a representative trace or example request in the tracing UI (trace id or link)
Metrics pipeline tags requests with: model_version, route, serving_path, io_mode, rollout_variant, and fallback_reason
Backfill job populates 90 days of historical latency summaries for high-traffic model/routes
SLO alert rule added for p99 regression per critical route with runbook referencing this dashboard
notes: Decision: prefer aggregated histograms in metrics backend (hdr histogram) over raw-percentile precomputation to reduce dimensional explosion
Trade-off: tagging by rollout_variant increases cardinality; we'll only tag for routes with active rollouts and sample the rest
Tracing hook design: add span attribute 'redwood.model.shard' and propagate request headers 'X-Redwood-Route' and 'X-Redwood-IO-Mode' into traces
Pipeline: metrics emitted from runtime -> datadog/prometheus bridge -> warehouse job to compute p50/p95/p99 daily and hourly aggregates
Temporary workaround: for private deployments with blocked telemetry, rely on agent-side aggregate metrics and optional customer-uploaded logs
